correctness.rationale: The inverse branches in x are h_0(x)=4/(5−x) and h_1(x)=4/(1+x); z=x/(4−x) sends them to (1+z)/4 and (1+z)/(4z) on J=[1/3,1]. The pushed-forward probability dz/(z log 3) is normalized and its two transfer contributions sum to 1/(z log 3). The composed inverse branches send the two endpoint columns of Q to the columns of K_w. They are nonsingular and their endpoint entries are positive, so every cylinder has positive measure and integrating the logarithmic density gives |log(ad/bc)|/log 3. The two explicit symmetric products M_jQ imply the full reversed product identity, not merely equality of selected short words. The branch boundary and its iterated preimages are null; reversal is of the stationary digit law, not invertibility of the interval map. The affine first branch fixes 1/3 and shrinks by 1/4, giving the exact all-zero cylinder formula. For t>0 the derivative of log(1+t/4)/log(1+t) has the sign of (1+t)log(1+t)/4−(1+t/4)log(1+t/4), which starts at zero and has strictly positive derivative. The all-zero continuation probabilities therefore strictly decrease to 1/4 and cannot be constant for histories sharing a finite last-m suffix. This also rules out independence. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its bounded word tests are not the general proof.
